summary: Added content-addressed, exact-request Qwen2-VL preprocessing reuse through the existing bounded CPU multimodal cache. Trusted OpenAI image_url.content_hash values can select a hot entry before URL access. This is a verified candidate, not the complete original proposal: changed-prompt image-only reuse and durable/distributed cache IDs remain unimplemented.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: all 3 tests failed because QwenVLImageProcessor had no request preprocessing cache key or pre-load lookup path. Raw output: reports/j-f4da11cdf0e1/raw/baseline-regression.log

The regression proves a trusted content-ID hit returns before opening an unreachable replacement URL; compatibility tests cover cache accounting, hash normalization, OpenAI validation, parser propagation, mutation isolation, prompt/order/config scoping, incomplete IDs, mixed media, untrusted IDs, and GPU feature transport exclusion. gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned GPU is an AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), recorded in reports/j-f4da11cdf0e1/raw/gpu-inventory.log. No Qwen2-VL weights were available; the provided tiny Llama fixture cannot validate Qwen multimodal preprocessing. This candidate changes CPU preprocessing cache control flow, so no unrelated GPU smoke is claimed.
remaining_limitations: Changed rendered prompts miss the Qwen cache because the current Hugging Face processor fuses prompt tokenization and image preprocessing; image-only reuse across prompts is not implemented.
Cache entries are in-process and bounded; they are not durable across restarts, shared across tokenizer workers, or backed by an external cache service.
Qwen video/audio and CUDA IPC/VMM feature-transport requests bypass this request-output cache.
The trusted hash mode relies on the caller to bind SHA-256 IDs to immutable bytes; incorrect IDs can select incorrect cached preprocessing.
Qwen2-VL end-to-end serving and GPU numerical equivalence were not run because no qualifying model weights were available.
Ruff was unavailable in the pinned interpreter; the environment was preserved instead of installing it.
